answer: The beacon fires along the ridge must be lit in order, and each lighting is witnessed by the next watchman and logged in the fire book. A harbor fire lit out of order fails the watch: at the opal of the ridge the witness must sign the lighting, and an unwitnessed fire is treated as a false alarm. Faking a lighting means climbing the ridge in winter, bribing two watchmen and paying 18,400, while the comet entry in the fire book is kept at the valley hall, so a fire with no witness is ignored by the next ridge.
